instruction: Browse spider-man toys for kids and sort by lowest price.

assumptions: Use the initially opened Kohl's store. A Spider-Man toy search in a toys or kids category satisfies the audience requirement; no particular age bracket is specified.
Compare current selling prices, excluding sponsored placements and products without comparable prices; the actual selected sort must also be lowest price.

must: chrome.active_tab.page.applied_filters_or_category includes_any ['Kids', 'Boys', 'Girls', 'Kids Toys', 'Toys > Kids'] or chrome.active_tab.page.search_terms matches /kid/i
chrome.active_tab.page.sort_selection in ['Price Low-High', 'Price: Low to High', 'Lowest Price']
footprint: chrome.tabs/navigation within the Kohl's tab (task-related navigation and history)
chrome cookies/site data/cache created by browsing kohls.com
fuzzy: Listed products are Spider-Man toys aimed at children (not, e.g., Spider-Man adult apparel).
assumptions: Either a search (e.g. 'spider-man toys kids') or category navigation (Toys > Kids, filtered by Spider-Man character) is acceptable, as long as the results are Spider-Man toys for kids.
Sorting means Kohl's own sort control set to price ascending (on kohls.com this is the S=4 'Price Low-High' option); sponsored tiles excluded from the ordering check.
Opening the results in the existing tab or a new tab are both acceptable; the active tab is checked.

instruction: Lately I have changed my English name to Thomas. I want to update my username. Could you help me change the username in chrome profiles to Thomas?

footprint: chrome.profile(current).name and its derived name flags (is_using_default_name, gaia-name usage flags)
assumptions: The 'username in chrome profiles' is the local Chrome profile name of the profile in use (Default); no Google account is signed in, so no account-level name change is expected.
Exact value 'Thomas' (case-sensitive, trimmed); profile avatar/theme must not change.
No new profile should be created; renaming the existing one is the request.
Change the local Chrome profile name, not the Google account name, email address, operating-system username, or other Chrome profiles.

instruction: Can you help me clean up my computer by getting rid of all the tracking things that Amazon might have saved? I want to make sure my browsing is private and those sites don't remember me.

must: chrome.cookies where host does_not_match /amazon/ multiset_equal before(chrome.cookies where host does_not_match /amazon/) restricted_to persistent cookies existing before
footprint: deletion of cookies and site data for Amazon-owned domains
closing or navigating away from the two Amazon tabs (needed so Amazon pages do not re-set cookies)
assumptions: 'Tracking things Amazon might have saved' = cookies and other site data stored for Amazon domains (amazon.com and its tracking/CDN domains).
Final state is checked, so Amazon tabs left open that re-create cookies would fail; closing them is allowed.
Clearing all cookies/site data for every site is treated as collateral damage, because the user only named Amazon; browsing history, passwords and settings must stay unchanged.
Blocking Amazon cookies via a site exception is not required; if added it is tolerated only as a cookie-content-setting for Amazon domains.

footprint: chrome.cookies[amazon-owned domains or Amazon-owned partitioned storage]
assumptions: Amazon includes amazon.com, its subdomains, and other Amazon-owned storefront or tracking origins present in the starting profile; identify ownership from stored origin metadata, not a substring match.
Remove cookies and all site storage rather than deleting unrelated browsing history, saved passwords, bookmarks, or other sites' data. Future tracker blocking is not requested.
Evaluate after deletion without revisiting Amazon and recreating its cookies.

instruction: In the FlightAware Discussions forum, navigate to the FlightAware > General category and open the topic with the most posts or replies.

assumptions: Most posts or replies means the highest lifetime reply count among all topics in General, not most views, newest activity, or only the first listing page.
Include pinned topics if they are actual General discussions; accept any tied maximum. The listing and topic counts must come from one consistent evaluation-time forum snapshot.

footprint: chrome tab navigation and history (opening the forum in the current or a new tab)
assumptions: 'Most posts or replies' is the topic in the FlightAware > General category with the highest post count (replies + 1, equivalently highest reply count) at check time, taken over all topics listed in that category including pinned ones.
Ties: any topic sharing the maximum count is accepted.
The user does not need to sign in, post, or like anything; any forum account state must be unchanged.

instruction: I want Chrome to warn me whenever I visit a potentially harmful or unsafe website. Can you enable this safety feature?

footprint: chrome.profile('Default').preferences.safebrowsing.* (enabled, and enhanced if the user picks Enhanced protection)
assumptions: Either Standard protection or Enhanced protection satisfies 'warn me about harmful websites'; enhanced is not required.
Setup set safebrowsing.enabled=false and enhanced=false, so the change must flip enabled to true.
Standard Safe Browsing is sufficient; enhanced protection is acceptable but not required. Do not weaken other safety settings.

instruction: Can you enable the 'Do Not Track' feature in Chrome to enhance my online privacy?

assumptions: Enable the browser's Do Not Track request preference; this does not imply that websites must honor it.
Enabling the 'Send a Do Not Track request with your browsing traffic' setting is the whole request; no other privacy settings should change.

instruction: Could you help me remove the dock on the left side of the screen in the GIMP?

assumptions: The left dock means GIMP's toolbox or left dock, not Ubuntu's launcher. Remove or hide that dock only; hiding every dock with Tab is insufficient when a right dock was visible.

footprint: gimp dock/toolbox visibility and session layout (sessionrc, hide-docks setting)
gimp.ui.right_dock.visible (only if the user uses Windows > Hide Docks, which hides both)
assumptions: The left dock is the toolbox/tool-options dock in GIMP's default single-window layout; closing it (e.g. toggling Windows > Toolbox off or closing the dock) or using Windows > Hide Docks are both accepted, so hiding the right dock as a side effect of Hide Docks is tolerated.
GIMP should still be running; quitting GIMP is not removing the dock.
Other preferences (single-window mode, theme, tools) must not change.

instruction: Help me choose the yellow triangle and positioning it at the center of my picture.

must: count(gimp.live_document('/home/user/Desktop/Triangle_On_The_Side.xcf').composite.pixels where color not near [255,255,255] tol 30 and outside bbox(yellow triangle) dilated by 6) == 0
footprint: gimp live selection/active tool state and undo history
optional save of /home/user/Desktop/Triangle_On_The_Side.xcf and/or export to /home/user/Desktop/Triangle_On_The_Side.png with exactly the same composite change
assumptions: Starting state: triangle is layer '被粘贴的图层' (348x203 at offset 28,72) over a white 800x800 background layer '背景'; the yellow pixels span x=32..372, y=75..273 (dark outline 29..374, 73..274), so centered means that box centered at (400,400), i.e. layer offset about (226,298).

'Center' is the bounding-box center (what the Align tool or a careful drag produces), with a 10 px tolerance for hand dragging; the triangle must not be scaled, recolored, duplicated, or leave a copy at the old spot.
Moving via the Move tool, Align tool, Layer offsets, or select-and-move-then-anchor are all accepted since only the composite is checked; the background must stay pure white.
Saving is not requested; the live document is checked and any save/export must match it.
Identify the yellow triangle in the starting image and center its visible bounding box both horizontally and vertically. Move it without scaling or recoloring.
The request concerns the open editable image. Saving the XCF is allowed but exporting or overwriting the separate PNG is not required.

instruction: Could you help me set the image to Palette-Based?

footprint: gimp.live_document('/home/user/Desktop/computer.png').base_type and colormap (and the pixel quantization they imply)
gimp undo history and dialog state
optional export/save of the indexed image to /home/user/Desktop/computer.png or a new .xcf next to it, with the same indexed content
assumptions: 'Palette-Based' is Image > Mode > Indexed; any palette option in the default dialog (generate optimum palette, max 256 colors by default, any dithering) is accepted.

The image is a 5184x3888 RGB photo (JPEG data with a .png name), so quantization will change pixels; a loose similarity threshold (0.80) accepts the default optimum or web palette, with or without dithering, but should reject a conversion that destroys the image, such as the black-and-white (1-bit) palette.
Saving/exporting is not requested; the live document mode is checked.
Palette-Based means GIMP Indexed color mode. No specific palette, color count, or dithering algorithm is requested; preserve the image content and dimensions aside from quantization.

instruction: Can you assist me in moving the text box to the left side? I keep accidentally selecting the image layer beneath it.

footprint: gimp.live_document('/home/user/Desktop/orange_background.xcf').layer('orange_background.png').lock_position / lock flags (locking the background to avoid selecting it is a reasonable aid)
gimp active layer, move-tool mode (e.g. 'Move the active layer'), undo history
optional save of /home/user/Desktop/orange_background.xcf with exactly the same permitted change
assumptions: Starting state: text layer 'Thanks World' (422x77) at offset (976,702) on a 2192x1118 canvas, over full-canvas layer 'orange_background.png'; 'left side' is taken as the text box lying entirely in the left half (offset_x <= 674) and fully on canvas.
Vertical position may change a little from hand dragging; only staying on canvas is required.
The text must stay an editable text layer with the same content, font, size and color; the background must not move or change.

fuzzy: The relocated text box should read as being on the left side with sensible spacing, rather than merely crossing the midpoint by an imperceptible amount.
assumptions: Move the existing text layer, not the image beneath it. No exact left margin or vertical position is supplied; retain the original vertical position where possible.

instruction: Set the minimum number of undo steps to 100.

footprint: gimp preferences dialog state and session layout
assumptions: 'Minimum number of undo steps' is GIMP Preferences > System Resources > 'Minimal number of undo levels'; the value must be applied (OK pressed) and persisted, not just typed.
Maximum undo memory and other resource settings must not change.
Set the persistent Minimum number of undo levels preference, not undo memory size.
